Professional Role, Competencies, and Issues for APRNs | Evidence-Based Practice & Clinical Guidelines
Clinical practice guidelines include recommendations intended to optimize patient care. Informed
by systematic review of the evidence and an assessment of the risks versus benefits.
Guideline development
1. Gather best available research evidence through a detailed literature search about the
appropriateness and effectiveness of different clinical strategies.
2. The research evidence is used for guideline construction by small groups who represent as
many interested parties as possible.
3. The guideline is then tested by professionals in select settings who were not involved in the
guideline development to review it for clarity, internal consistency, and acceptability.
4. The guideline should be reviewed at specified periods of time and modified when new
knowledge is gained.

1 Systemic reviews and Combines the results of multiple original studies (systematic review)
meta-analysis or independent trials (meta-analysis) to produce an overall result. A
systematic review will often include a meta-analysis. Meta-analysis can
be done on any selection of results, but it is only regarded as level 1
evidence if combined with a systematic review.
2 Randomized controlled Trial participants are randomly assigned to either a control group or a
trials treatment group who receive a specific intervention. The aim is to control
all other factors that may influence the effect of the intervention.
3 Cohort studies Two or more groups of people who have a different exposure to a
particular agent (like smoking, a vaccine, or type of surgery) are selected
and then followed up to see what differences there are between the
groups for specific outcomes.
4 Case-control studies People with a particular condition (cases) are matched with people
without the condition (controls), and differences are then examined in a
retrospective analysis.
5 Cross-sectional Studies An examination of a sample of the population of interest at one point in
time. Surveys often use a questionnaire or interview design.
6 Case reports A report based on a single patient which can sometimes be collected
into a short series.
7 Expert opinion A consensus from the experts in the field.
8 Anecdotal Observations made through clinical practice which link a particular
outcome with a particular condition or intervention.
